arxiv-2201-12803.title: Generalizing similarity in noisy setups: the DIBS phenomenon
arxiv-2201-12803.creator: Nayara Fonseca ∗,, Veronica Guidetti ∗,
arxiv-2201-12803.description: Abstract This work uncovers an interplay among data density, noise, and the generalization ability in similarity learning. We consider Siamese Neural Networks (SNNs), which are the basic form of contrastive learning, and explore two types of noise that can impact SNNs, Pair Label Noise (PLN) and Single Label Noise (SLN).

arxiv-2206-14235.title: Isospin-symmetry implications for nuclear two-body distributions and short-range correlations
arxiv-2206-14235.creator: Ronen Weiss a {}^{\,{\rm a}} , Alessandro Lovato b , c , d {}^{\,{\rm b,c,d}} , R. B. Wiringa b {}^{\,{\rm b}}
arxiv-2206-14235.description: Abstract We study the implications of isospin symmetry in nuclear systems on two-body distributions and derive relations between different densities or momentum distributions of a given nucleus or of different nuclei in the same isospin multiplet. A connection between neutrinoless double beta decay transition of mirror nuclei and two-body densities is also obtained.

arxiv-2210-11642.title: Improving Semi-supervised End-to-end Automatic Speech Recognition using CycleGAN and Inter-domain Losses
arxiv-2210-11642.creator: Chia-Yu Li, Ngoc Thang Vu
arxiv-2210-11642.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Chia-Yu Li, Ngoc Thang Vu. We propose a novel method that combines CycleGAN and inter-domain losses for semi-supervised end-to-end automatic speech recognition. Inter-domain loss targets the extraction of an intermediate shared representation of speech and text inputs using a shared network. CycleGAN uses cycle-consistent loss and the identity mapping loss to preserve relevant characteristics of the input feature after converting from one domain to another. As such, both approaches are suitable to train end-to-end models on unpaired speech-text inputs.

arxiv-2302-03173.title: Learning bias corrections for climate models using deep neural operators
arxiv-2302-03173.creator: Aniruddha Bora, Khemraj Shukla, Shixuan Zhang, Bryce Harrop, Ruby Leung, George Em Karniadakis
arxiv-2302-03173.description: Abstract Numerical simulation for climate modeling resolving all important scales is a computationally taxing process. Therefore, to circumvent this issue a low resolution simulation is performed, which is subsequently corrected for bias using reanalyzed data (ERA5), known as nudging correction.

arxiv-2307-00357.title: Abstract Orientable Incidence Structure and Algorithms for Finite Bounded Acyclic Categories. II. Data Structure and Fundamental Operations
arxiv-2307-00357.creator: Yu-Wei Huang
arxiv-2307-00357.description: Abstract A data structure for finite bounded acyclic categories has been built, which is useful to encode and manipulate abstract orientable incidence structure. It can be represented as a directed acyclic multigraph with weighted edges, where the weighs encode the algebraic structure between edges. The fundamental operations on this data structure are investigated from geometrical, categorical and programming perspectives.

arxiv-2406-13737.title: The Born regime of gravitational amplitudes
arxiv-2406-13737.creator: Miguel Correia, and Giulia Isabella
arxiv-2406-13737.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Miguel Correia, and Giulia Isabella. We study the 2 → 2 2\to 2 scattering in the regime where the wavelength of the scattered objects is comparable to their distance but is much larger than any Compton wavelength in the quantum field theory. We observe that in this regime - which differs from the eikonal - the Feynman diagram expansion takes the form of a geometric series, akin to the Born series of quantum mechanics.

Corresponding author: Fan Liu. Thanks: This work was partially supported by the Fundamental Research Funds for the Central Universities (No. B240
arxiv-2412-12603.creator: 1 st Guangwenjie Zou, 1 st Liang Yao, 3 rd Fan Liu, 4 th Chuanyi Zhang, 5 th Xin Li, 6 th Ning Chen, 7 th Shengxiang Xu, 8 th Jun Zhou
arxiv-2412-12603.description: Abstract Since high resolution remote sensing image classification often requires a relatively high computation complexity, lightweight models tend to be practical and efficient. Model pruning is an effective method for model compression. However, existing methods rarely take into account the specificity of remote sensing images, resulting in significant accuracy loss after pruning.

pmc-11536178.title: Substrate specificity controlled by the exit site of human P4-ATPases, revealed by de novo point mutations in neurological disorders
pmc-11536178.creator: David C. Calianese, Tomoyasu Noji, Jennifer A. Sullivan, Kelly Schoch, Vandana Shashi, Vanda McNiven, Luiza Lorena Pires Ramos, Albena Jordanova, Judit Kárteszi, Hiroshi Ishikita, Shigekazu Nagata
pmc-11536178.description: SignificanceATPase 11A (ATP11A) is a flippase that specifically translocates phosphatidylserine from the outer to the inner leaflet of plasma membranes. We previously reported that a point mutation at its exoplasmic site causes the aberrant translocation of phosphatidylcholine (PtdCho), leading to the upregulation of a sphingomyelin (SM) synthetase and the accumulation of SM in the outer leaflet of the plasma membrane.

pmc-12633791.title: Broad H3K4me3 domains support oocyte genome silencing and maturation but are dispensable for repression in early embryos
pmc-12633791.creator: Trine Skuland, Madeleine Fosslie, Sherif Khodeer, Endalkachew Ashenafi Alemu, Jens Vilstrup Johansen, Marie Indahl, Blanca Corral Castroviejo, Yanjiao Li, Mads Lerdrup, John Arne Dahl, Peter Zoltan Fedorcsak, Gareth D Greggains
pmc-12633791.description: Epigenetic reprogramming and embryonic genome activation (EGA) are crucial events during early development. Establishment of distinctive broad histone H3 lysine 4 trimethylation (H3K4me3) domains in the oocyte is necessary for genome silencing, and their removal in the 2-cell embryo is crucial for EGA and development in mice. However, the stage-specific requirement for broad H3K4me3 domains is unclear.

pmc-12748879.title: Effect of early goal directed mobilization on clinical outcomes in mechanically ventilated ICU patients
pmc-12748879.creator: Wanzhu Zhang, Peilin Yu, Mengting Yu, Jie Mi
pmc-12748879.description: Patients with mechanical ventilation (MV) in the ICU are prone to various complications. It was proved that early mobility was effective, it improve functional status in patients with chronic diseases, and reduce disability. This study aimed to investigate the effects of early goal-directed mobilization (EGDM) on clinical outcomes of MV patients in ICU.

uslaw-usc-t18-s342.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part I (Crimes); Chapter 17A (Common Carrier Operation Under The Influence Of Alcohol Or Drugs). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Whoever operates or directs the operation of a common carrier while under the influence of alcohol or any controlled substance (as defined in section 102 of the Controlled Substances Act (21 U.S.C. 802)).

uslaw-usc-t22-s2734h.title: 22 U.S.C. § 2734h — Increased accountability in assignment restrictions and reviews
uslaw-usc-t22-s2734h.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t22-s2734h.description: United States Code, Title 22 (Foreign Relations And Intercourse); Chapter 38 (Department Of State). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Sense of Congress It is the sense of Congress that— (1) the use of policies to restrict personnel from serving in certain assignments may undermine the Department’s ability to deploy relevant cultural and linguistic skills at diplomatic posts abroad if not applied.

uslaw-usc-t33-s883k.title: 33 U.S.C. § 883k — Acquisition of land for facilities
uslaw-usc-t33-s883k.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t33-s883k.description: United States Code, Title 33 (Navigation And Navigable Waters); Chapter 17 (National Oceanic And Atmospheric Administration); Subchapter II (Surveys). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. For fiscal year 1990 and hereafter funds appropriated under this heading shall be available for acquisition of land for facilities.

uslaw-usc-t54-s100505.title: 54 U.S.C. § 100505 — Periodic review of System
uslaw-usc-t54-s100505.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t54-s100505.description: United States Code, Title 54 (National Park Service And Related Programs); Chapter 1005 (Areas Of National Park System). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Authority of Secretary To Conduct Review.— The Secretary shall conduct a systematic and comprehensive review of certain aspects of the System and on a periodic basis (but not less often than every 3 years) submit to the Committee.
